query: What is the schedule and status of Gaza second-phase negotiations in Cairo/Doha in August-September 2026? Are there planned summits, deadlines, or Board of Peace meetings before September 10, 2026 at which Israel might formally accept the 15-point plan?
answer:
## Summary

The research is complete and submitted. The decisive findings for the forecast:

**Israel has already formally rejected the plan and has not reversed it.** Netanyahu's Aug 9 statement was unusually explicit and deliberately repeated ("I have heard people saying: 'You didn't say it.' So here I am saying it again"). He reaffirmed the position at the Aug 17 Kushner meeting.

**Three structural facts work against acceptance by Sept 10:**

1. **No venue exists.** No Board of Peace plenary, summit, or signing event is scheduled in the window. UNGA's high-level week falls *after* the deadline (Sept 22–28; only the procedural opening is Sept 8). The only possible venues are the routine Sunday cabinet meetings of Aug 23, Aug 30, and Sept 6.

2. **Acceptance is immediately operative, not symbolic.** The annex BBC reviewed requires IDF withdrawal to the Yellow Line within 24 hours of Israeli government approval — which is exactly what Netanyahu is refusing, seven weeks before an election he is polling to lose.

3. **The US has stopped asking.** The most important dynamic is that Washington reshaped the process around Israel's refusal rather than confronting it — substituting working groups and a US-general verification mechanism, and flipping the roadmap's synchronized sequencing to Israel's disarmament-first ordering. A senior US official: "We understand Bibi's political needs. We have no problem with it as long as he continues to do what we ask."

**The main counter-consideration** is that Israel is substantively complying while publicly refusing — the Board of Peace has praised Israeli adherence, contradicting Netanyahu. But this arguably *lowers* the probability of formal acceptance: the current arrangement gives both sides what they need without it.

One flag for the forecaster: the roadmap defines no signing ceremony or ratification vote for itself, so "formal acceptance" has no canonical form. If Israel endorses a rebranded sequencing framework derived from the Aug 17 understandings, whether that resolves YES depends on the question's exact wording — worth checking against the resolution criteria.

key_facts: Israel formally rejected the 15-point plan on Aug 9, 2026: Netanyahu at a televised cabinet meeting said 'I wish to be precise here: Israel does not accept the 15-point document.' He has not reversed this as of Aug 19, 2026.

The Board of Peace published the 15-point 'Roadmap for Completing the Implementation of President Trump's Comprehensive Peace Plan in Gaza' on July 30, 2026 (full text July 31). Hamas and Palestinian factions accepted it; Israel did not.

The roadmap specifies NO signing ceremony, vote, or ratification mechanism for itself. It refers only to 'all parties approve the Roadmap' as the trigger starting a 14-day clock for the Phase 2 timetable (Art. 2) and the weapons-decommissioning timetable (Art. 8), both extendable by the International Verification Committee.

The BBC reported seeing an annex requiring Israeli forces to withdraw to the Yellow Line 'within 24 hours of the Israeli government's approval of the plan' - making formal acceptance immediately operative, not symbolic.

NO Board of Peace summit, plenary, Cairo/Doha summit, or signing event is scheduled between Aug 19 and Sept 10, 2026. The Board of Peace announcements page's most recent entry is July 30, 2026, with no forward calendar.
UNGA 81 opens Sept 8, 2026 (procedural only); the high-level General Debate runs Sept 22-28, 2026 - after the Sept 10 deadline.

Aug 16, 2026: Kushner, Mladenov and Blair held an unprecedented 2+ hour direct meeting with a Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya in Egypt (Cairo/El-Alamein), with Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish mediators. Kushner also met President Sisi.

Aug 17, 2026: Kushner, Mladenov, Blair and Amb. Huckabee met Netanyahu in Jerusalem for ~4 hours. Israeli participants included Shin Bet chief David Zini and military intelligence chief Shlomi Binder.

The Aug 17 meeting produced two joint working groups (disarmament/demilitarization; sanitation/clean water/public health), an understanding that US Maj. Gen. Jasper Jeffers would supervise weapons handover and destruction, and a deconfliction mechanism - but NOT Israeli acceptance of the roadmap. AP: 'no concrete commitment by Israel.' Guardian: 'no breakthrough.'

The Aug 17 understandings invert the roadmap's core logic: the document required synchronized phased disarmament and phased Israeli withdrawal; the new formula is disarmament first, withdrawal later. Washington moved toward Israel's position, not vice versa.
Per CNN, Netanyahu told Kushner and Mladenov that progress on the 15-point framework was politically 'problematic' ahead of Israel's October 27 election.
Israeli elections are set for October 27, 2026 - the last legally possible date. The Knesset dissolved July 17, 2026, completing the first full four-year term since 1988.

Since July 17, 2026 Israel has operated as a caretaker government with, per Xinhua, 'limited authority to advance major policy initiatives except for broadly supported legislation, routine regulatory matters and measures required for security needs.'
Channel 12 polling: Eizenkot's Yashar 23 seats, Likud 22, Bennett-Lapid 'Together' 16. Anti-Netanyahu bloc 59, pro-Netanyahu bloc 51, Arab parties 10 - neither bloc reaches the 61 needed.

Smotrich publicly claimed credit for the Aug 9 rejection ('I congratulate the Prime Minister for responding to our demand'). Ben Gvir called the deal 'unacceptable' and was the sole cabinet vote against ISF deployment. Smotrich's Religious Zionism is polling below the 3.25% electoral threshold and he has ruled out re-merging with Ben Gvir.

The White House is 'not bothered' by the rejection, viewing it as election-season rhetoric. A senior US official to Axios: 'We understand Bibi's political needs. We have no problem with it as long as he continues to do what we ask - especially regarding restraining attacks in Gaza.'

Kushner said on Fox News (Aug 17) that weapons-removal progress could come 'in as little as 30 days' (~Sept 16, after the deadline) and tunnel filling in '60 to 90 days.' His ultimatum framing was directed at Hamas, not Israel. No deadline or ultimatum has been issued to Israel.

Eight Arab and Muslim states (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Egypt, Qatar, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkiye) issued a joint statement on Aug 16 condemning Israel's rejection as threatening to derail Trump's efforts.

Counter-signal: Al-Monitor reports Israel is 'quietly implementing' the plan while publicly rejecting it - the cabinet authorized ISF entry July 26, the IDF suspended targeting of Hamas militants under US pressure, and airstrikes halted Aug 3 to ~Aug 11. The Board of Peace publicly praised Israel's adherence, contradicting Netanyahu's own statement.

Analyst consensus is that acceptance before the October election is very unlikely. Aaron David Miller: 'It's hard to believe that you're going to see any serious movement before you have another Israeli government.' Shira Efron (RAND): 'borderline impossible for the Israeli government to accept [the plan]' before elections. Yossi Kuperwasser: 'no movement prior to [the] end of October.'
